purpose: Submission plan only: what moves an acceptance decision, in what order, and the pre-registered acceptance test for each. Cell-level mechanism state, closed gaps and the retired v7 ledger live in docs/audit/todo-history.md and docs/audit/todo-archive-2026-10-27.json. The win definition and the decision rule are carried over verbatim; what changed is the ordering rule: work is ranked by how much it moves an acceptance decision, not by which cell is still losing.
objective: The framework must WIN on every model task: R1 (LineageFlow hmmscan hits), R2 (Kanzi RMSD), R3 (FlowMol3 fg_dev), R5a (2D FM W2), R5b (CIFAR FID), R5c (MNIST FID), R6 (LineageFlow scPerplexity/pLDDT), K1 (FlowMol3 pb_validity), K7 (LineageFlow novelty). A TIE is a loss. A LOSS is an open mechanism gap, not a boundary to be published. Every cell that is not a win today has a mechanism gap below whose acceptance test is that win.
submission_objective: Publish in a CAS tier-1 (中科院一区) journal, TNNLS first. The paper is packaged and submittable as of 2026-10-27 (12 pages, 0 overfull, 3 STRONG + 1 CONDITIONAL + 1 TIE + 2 PARTIAL + 4 SUPP-only). What it lacks is not prose but one piece of evidence: the central claim is currently a four-point cross-section, and the reviewer's first objection is already known. The plan below exists to convert that cross-section into an identification, then to put it in the paper.
win_definition: A cell wins only if BOTH hold. (1) POINT WIN: at the cell's canonical protocol (same checkpoint, same N, same seeds), the framework's metric is better with the paired 95% CI excluding 0 and clearing the cell's alpha. (2) FRONTIER DOMINANCE: over the NFE grid, the framework's (quality, NFE) curve lies at or below the baseline's at every grid point, and the framework's plateau is better than the baseline's plateau. (2) is the load-bearing one: flow-matching inference saturates with steps, so 'the baseline with more steps' is NOT a valid control and NOT a threat -- the baseline's ceiling is fixed by its own inference protocol. The framework's claim is that it raises that ceiling AND reaches a given quality at fewer NFE. Both halves are measured, not asserted.
frontier_protocol: Per model: baseline and framework on the SAME checkpoint, prior, seed policy and N, swept over NFE in {10, 25, 50, 100, 200} (extended upward until the baseline plateaus for two consecutive points). Report per-NFE paired deltas with CIs, the plateau estimate (mean of the last two grid points), and the dominance verdict. A cell whose baseline does not plateau on the grid has an unfinished ceiling measurement, not a win.
recording_policy: Observations-only: write audit docs + todo.json + raw artifacts. Frozen CLAIMS.md / CONSOLIDATED_RESULTS.md / paper-A-final.* / tnnls_submission/** stay untouched without explicit user authorization.
decision_rule: An experiment runs only if it can change a claim's STATUS or a metric's MAGNITUDE. More seeds, more draws or a larger N on an already-measured effect do not qualify: they buy confidence, not strength. When a cell is power-limited or negative, stop measuring and strengthen the adapter: study the domain (the upstream implementation, the metric's own definition, the field's validity rules), write the design hypothesis down, change the code, then make ONE pre-registered measurement. A tie is a loss and is treated as an open gap. Seed top-ups after a run are forbidden in every case; a cell's canonical seed set is fixed in its pre-registration before the first number exists.
research_protocol: 1) Read the upstream implementation of the state space being perturbed (channel geometry, latent geometry, embedding geometry) before proposing anything.
2) Read the metric's definition and the scorer, not just its name: what does it reward, and would it reward the change we are about to make for a trivial reason?
3) State the design hypothesis as a falsifiable sentence with the expected sign and rough size, in the audit doc, BEFORE touching code.
4) Change one mechanism at a time; keep the old arm runnable so the before/after is paired on the same seed and the same prior.
5) One confirmatory measurement at the cell's canonical N/NFE/seeds. No seed top-ups afterwards.

6) Never frame the control as 'the baseline with more steps'. Flow-matching inference saturates in the step count, so the baseline's ceiling is set by its own inference protocol; the correct control is the baseline at its plateau, and the claim to prove is (quality, NFE) frontier dominance plus a higher plateau.
gate_note: The pytest entry is the fast canonical subset. Full pytest is run per change: 15 known failures (3 stale eval stubs; 12 order-dependent test_paper_metrics cases). docs-vs-code verifies 3371 claims since the 2026-10-27 packaging pass.

venue_assessment.note: Judgment, not measurement. Recorded so the ordering below can be argued with.

drivers_against: the only large effect is on a 5k-step MNIST checkpoint; three better-trained checkpoints tie

venue_assessment.timing_risk: TNNLS first review can take 6-12 months. Waiting for reviewer feedback before running GAP-90 therefore risks an 18-24 month total cycle, which is why GAP-90 is ordered first.

execution_order: 1. GAP-90-EPOCH-DOSE-CONTROLLED (P0) - the identification experiment. Same architecture, same training set, only epochs vary; five levels. Two days on one GPU. Nothing else moves the acceptance estimate as much.
2. GAP-91-FLOOR-DISTANCE-LAW (P0, depends on GAP-90) - turn the measured relation into an out-of-sample predictor, or reject it.

3. GAP-92-KAPPA-BRIDGE-INTO-PAPER (P1, no GPU) - GAP-78 already measured a contraction that orders the sign; the manuscript currently says no such thing exists. Put the measured relation in, with its scope.
4. GAP-93-CONVERGED-CHECKPOINT-LEVER (P1) - production is a near-miss (-0.50 FID, CI [-0.9996, +0.0025]) not a wall. One pre-registered mechanism change.
5. GAP-94-STANDARD-BENCHMARK (P1, USER GATE) - one competitive image benchmark at matched NFE. Needs a decision on model access and compute.
6. GAP-95-FRONTIER-GRIDS-REMAINING (P2) - every R-level cell gets a grid or a measured reason it cannot have one.
7. GAP-96-MANUSCRIPT-COMPRESSION (P2) - cut engineering bulk to make room for the GAP-90 figure and the GAP-92 table; hold 12 pages.
8. GAP-15-VENUE-AND-TIMING (P1, user) - submit now, or run GAP-90 first. The estimate above assumes GAP-90 runs first.

open_gaps.gap: The paper's central claim is that the gain from re-inference is checkpoint-conditional. The evidence is four MNIST checkpoints (w16e1_5k, 10k, 60k, production) that differ in architecture, training-set size and training time at once. That is a cross-section. A reviewer can accept every number and still reject the inference.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: Under a controlled axis - same architecture, same training set, only the number of training epochs varies - the framework's plateau gain decreases monotonically with training completeness, because the gain is the baseline's distance to its own floor (GAP-84 reading). Expected size, from the distance-to-floor relation: about -3 FID at a baseline plateau near 24, about -1 FID near 17, and within the 1-FID floor at or below 11. Sign: negative everywhere, magnitude shrinking.
open_gaps.research: 1) Pin the family: one MNIST FM architecture, one training set (60k), epochs E in {1, 2, 5, 10, 20}, three training seeds each. 2) Verify each checkpoint's baseline plateau actually descends across NFE (a checkpoint whose single pass has already converged cannot carry the test). 3) Frontier per checkpoint at N=1000 per arm, sampling seeds 42/43/44, rungs {4,5,10,25,50,100,200}, --min-steps-per-round 2, headline arm evidence_driven, plateau = mean of the last two rungs. 4) Report the per-checkpoint plateau delta with its 95% CI and the floor verdict.
open_gaps.acceptance: All three, or the law is rejected and the manuscript keeps its current hypothesis wording. (a) The plateau gain is non-increasing in E across the five levels, with the OLS slope's 95% CI excluding 0. (b) At E=1 the cell reproduces the WIN under the controlled axis: 7/7 strict rung gains and a plateau CI that clears the 1-FID floor. (c) At E=20 the cell ties inside the floor - the same verdict as production today, but now on a checkpoint that differs from E=1 only in training time.
open_gaps.est_wall: 2 days on cuda:0; about 210 N=1000 cells (5 checkpoints x 3 training seeds x 7 rungs x 2 arms)
open_gaps.agent_action: Write docs/audit/gap90-epoch-dose.md first - hypothesis, sign, expected size, the exact checkpoint list, the acceptance test above - and commit it BEFORE the first sample. Then train, then sweep, then tools/frontier_report.py per checkpoint, then record.

open_gaps.gap: GAP-84 recorded that the gain tracks the baseline's distance to its own floor, but only as a description of four points. A description is a caveat; a predictor is a result.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: The plateau gain is a function of the baseline plateau's distance to the checkpoint family's floor, and that function predicts the sign and rough size on a checkpoint family it was not fitted on.
open_gaps.research: Fit the relation on the GAP-90 five points plus the four GAP-84 checkpoints; hold out one family (Kanzi reconstruction, or CIFAR-10 FID) and test the prediction there. Report the fit, the held-out error, and the sign agreement.
open_gaps.acceptance: Out-of-sample sign correct on every held-out checkpoint AND |predicted - observed| below 1 FID, the paper's floor unit. Otherwise the relation is reported as descriptive only and the paper says so.
open_gaps.est_wall: no GPU; re-analysis of existing artifacts plus one held-out cell
open_gaps.agent_action: Write the fit and the held-out protocol into the GAP-90 audit as a second section; do not open a separate artifact tree.

open_gaps.gap: The manuscript states that the two theorems do not determine the sign of an FID change. That is true of the theorems as stated. But GAP-78 measured a contraction (kappa) that does order the sign - 12/12 weak dominance at beta=0.3 on the floor rule - and that measurement is not in the paper. A reviewer reads 'the theory does not predict' as 'the theory is decorative', which is worse than the truth.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: The measured contraction orders the sign of the plateau delta across checkpoints, even though the theorem alone does not. Reporting it converts the theory section from decoration into a diagnostic with a measured hit rate.
open_gaps.research: Compute kappa per checkpoint from the existing diagnostics; tabulate kappa against the observed plateau delta for the four GAP-84 checkpoints and the five GAP-90 checkpoints. State the rule with its scope: measured on MNIST FM at beta=0.3 under one floor rule.
open_gaps.acceptance: A table with at least four checkpoints, and a manuscript paragraph whose every clause is backed by a number in that table. Hard constraint: the paragraph must not claim the theorem predicts FID - only that the measured kappa orders it on this family.
open_gaps.est_wall: no GPU; one re-analysis plus a manuscript edit
open_gaps.agent_action: Read docs/audit/gap78-dispersion-gate.md and verification_outputs/gap78-kappa-dose-n1000-3seed/ before writing a single sentence.
